explanation: Pull Requests are the fundamental collaboration unit on GitHub.
tip: Even solo developers open PRs to self-review before merging to main.

explanation: Double check your base branch! Merging into the wrong branch can cause unexpected deployment issues.
You can click on any line number in the diff to leave a comment on that exact line.
tip: Reviewers can also start a multi-line review.

explanation: Just `git add`, `git commit`, and `git push`. The PR timeline updates automatically.
tip: No need to close or recreate the PR.

explanation: Draft PRs clearly signal: 'I am still writing code, but take a look if you want'.
tip: Convert to 'Ready for review' when done.

explanation: Squash & Merge is popular because it keeps `main` history clean and easy to read.
tip: Teams usually agree on one standard merge strategy in their repo settings.

explanation: Squashing turns 10 'fix typo' commits into one clean 'feat: add profile page' commit.
tip: It preserves a spotless commit history on main.

explanation: Review the code, not the person. Use phrases like 'What do you think about...' or 'Could we optimize this by...'.
tip: Empathy and clear communication make great teams.

explanation: The author can click 'Commit suggestion' to immediately accept your fix without opening their editor.
tip: A huge time saver during reviews.

explanation: `git switch main && git pull` completes the circle.
tip: Clean up the old feature branch locally with `git branch -d <name>`.
